headline: Marcos Urges Filipinos to Draw Courage and Unity from Ninoy Aquino’s Legacy
seoTitle: Marcos: Draw Courage from Ninoy's Legacy | FMB News
seoDescription: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. issued a Ninoy Aquino Day message on August 21 urging Filipinos to draw courage, conviction and unity from the late senator’s legacy.
deck: The President’s holiday message framed Ninoy Aquino’s legacy around courage, conviction and national unity as commemorations marked the 43rd anniversary of his assassination.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. issued a Ninoy Aquino Day message on Friday, August 21, calling on Filipinos to draw courage, conviction and unity from the legacy of former Senator Benigno ‘Ninoy’ Aquino Jr., according to the approved FMB News evening brief.
Aquino was assassinated on August 21, 1983. The annual observance remains a major civic and historical commemoration tied to the country’s democratic history.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The message comes from a President whose family history is directly intertwined with the political era in which Aquino became the leading opposition figure. For that reason, wording around the commemoration carries unusual historical and political weight.

FMB News is presenting the President’s message as an official commemorative statement, not as a resolution of competing historical interpretations about the Martial Law period or the Aquino-Marcos political conflict.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Presidential commemorative messages help signal how the administration chooses to frame contested national memory. Emphasizing courage and unity places the focus on civic lessons and shared national purpose rather than partisan conflict.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch how political leaders, civil-society groups, educators and historians respond to the administration’s framing of Ninoy Aquino’s legacy and how the message is used in future official commemorations.
